0x140010.why: a protection bank probe: the 0x140000 window is served by a state machine, and what the chip FETCHES there depends on the access sequence - the forced-PC capture executed it as moveq #2 (the live bank) while every byte-wise READ of the window, including the io capture itself, returns the moveq #0 image prog_ext.bin holds. The port pins that read-view bank and returns 0. The caller at 0xEDEA uses d0 to seed the difficulty table when the difficulty byte is out of range - protection sabotage; 0 is a safe clamp. The case measures protection state, not translation

0x1400e4.why: the other half of the protection pair: it cmpm-compares a table at 0x1432A0 in the board ROM against the program image, and that window is served by the same state machine as its sibling at 0x140010 - what a fetch sees there depends on the access sequence, so the frozen io snapshot the harness serves is one bank and the chip under the capture was reading another. The port's lift matches the read-view image; the case measures protection state, not translation

0x1996a.why: base of a descending byte table: three routines read load8(0x1996a + index) and fn_19a24 walks it backwards with post-decrement loads; the host routine's own flow at 0x19966 branches over these bytes; lifted as a function it is or-noise ending in a movep with a wild displacement

0x13dda.why: month-name table JANFEBMAR...DEC followed by a days-per-month byte table (0x1f/0x1e), read by the self-test clock display; real code resumes at the movem.l at 0x13e0a; the citation was a junk block fabricated from the table's first bytes after the host's closing bra.b at 0x13dd4

0x197f4.why: complete routine: signed halving and negation of a stacked step (asr/neg/ext.l/add.l on 4(a7) and a(a7)), runs to its rts; nothing known reaches it - unreached code, not data

0x19b06.why: complete routine behind twelve bytes of table (ffff ff00 ff01 ...): loads 0(a2), early-out beq, walks a structure through a3; the data prefix 0x19af4-0x19b06 stays data; nothing known reaches it

0x767c.why: complete function with link/movem prologue: copies a two-byte key to the frame, walks a list comparing a 6-bit field (andi #$3f) against the key; nothing known reaches it

0x16958.why: complete function with link/movem prologue in the service-mode cluster: loads three word arguments, 180 as a limit, accumulates through a loop; nothing known reaches it

0xe562.why: counter-clamp pair: pea 1/pea $13, call the read thunk at 0x178, if above 2000 write 2000 back through the thunk at 0x18a; twin at 0xe588 does counter $12; nothing known reaches either

0xe588.why: second member of the counter-clamp pair at 0xe562, for counter $12

0x1e834.why: the crash screen's column fill: writes a byte four times through (a1)+, skips 0x1fc to the next playfield row group, eight groups; complete to its rts at 0x1e858; nothing lifted cites it, so either the dump's deeper blocks were pruned or it is dead - unreached code either way

0x19af4.why: the eighteen bytes before the routine at 0x19b06: three ff-words of table then movep-flavoured junk around an accidental rts; markers 5.56 is six words doing their worst

0x11e7e.why: ori-noise with undecodable words and branches to misaligned neighbourhoods; marker score 1.09 is the accident of 92 bytes, not a prologue; sits between the dissolve and RNG routines as their table

ranges.why: the exception stubs' message text: each stub is one jsr to 0x18652, which prints the text after the jsr through the stacked return address and jumps to the halt stub at 0x1e8d2 - the call never returns, so a lifted fall-through target inside this range is the message, not code

the upper program image: pictures and their tables. Zero control transfers from any routine land here, opcode-marker density is 0.00 per 100 bytes across 917504 bytes (real code runs 2-6), and the art tooling decodes graphics from it; the 24610 aligned values that look like overlay pointers are what a million bytes of art encodes by accident

the board ROM, pictures plus the protection furniture, except the two measured code islands the map carries: 0x140010 (moveq #0; rts) and 0x1400e4-0x14010e (the table compare). The knock addresses the power-on probe reads (0x140000, 0x1400a8, 0x1400e8, 0x1432b0, 0x1460xx) and the table at 0x140034 are data the code touches, not code

a byte-wide device on the odd byte lane: every one of the 14336 nonzero bytes in the io-baseline capture sits at an odd address, and the two 64KB halves are identical - a mirrored byte device, the settings/bookkeeping store. No transfer lands here and marker density is zero. The port reads the captured bytes and discards writes (machine.ts)
